code:
# keep LimitCORE=infinity in the unit; give every container the rlimit through the runc handler of the CRI plugin: a copy of the default OCI spec with RLIMIT_CORE 0/0, set as base_runtime_spec
ctr oci spec | sudo python3 -c "
import json, sys
s = json.load(sys.stdin)
s['process']['rlimits'] = [r for r in s['process'].get('rlimits', []) if r['type'] != 'RLIMIT_CORE'] + [{'type': 'RLIMIT_CORE', 'hard': 0, 'soft': 0}]
json.dump(s, open('/etc/bench72094271/base-spec.json', 'w'))
"
sudo sed -i "s#^\( *base_runtime_spec = \).*#\1'/etc/bench72094271/base-spec.json'#" /etc/bench72094271/containerd.toml
sudo systemctl restart bench72094271-containerd.service

# what the asker did first: the unit file is edited and the service restarted, but systemd keeps the unit it loaded before
sudo sed -i 's/^LimitCORE=.*/LimitCORE=0/' /etc/systemd/system/bench72094271-containerd.service
sudo systemctl restart bench72094271-containerd.service

# soft 0, hard infinity: the main process shows 'ulimit -c' 0, but any process can raise it again
sudo mkdir -p /etc/systemd/system/bench72094271-containerd.service.d
printf '[Service]\nLimitCORE=0:infinity\n' | sudo tee /etc/systemd/system/bench72094271-containerd.service.d/10-core.conf >/dev/null
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl restart bench72094271-containerd.service

# the new containers inherit from the running containerd, but nothing of the service changed: the next restart brings infinity back
sudo prlimit --core=0:0 --pid "$(systemctl show -p MainPID --value bench72094271-containerd.service)"

# containerd leaves the service: the process that answers on the socket is not the main process of the unit
sudo systemctl stop bench72094271-containerd.service
sudo setsid -f prlimit --core=0:0 containerd --config /etc/bench72094271/containerd.toml >/tmp/bench72094271-hand.log 2>&1 </dev/null
sleep 3

# no core file anywhere, but the limit of the containers is still unlimited
sudo sysctl -w kernel.core_pattern=/dev/null
